meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots + dull skin**, I’d start with a **10% vitamin C serum**, rather than jumping straight to 15–20%. Stable vitamin-C derivatives such as 3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid are generally easier to tolerate, while 10–15% is a practical range for brightening. **🥇 Best overall for a beginner: Minimalist 10% Vitamin C**  
A good choice if your main goals are gradual fading of dark marks and brighter, more even-looking skin. Current shopping results show it around ₹269–₹629 depending on seller/variant. [phdbeauty.com](https://phdbeauty.com/blogs/general-advice/best-vitamin-c-serum-india-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.pingmedoc.com](https://www.pingmedoc.com/pharmacy/buying-guides/best-vitamin-c-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥈 If you've already used vitamin C: Plum 15% Vitamin C**  
A stronger option for someone whose skin already tolerates vitamin C. The current listing is around ₹457. 

**🥉 If you want a stronger antioxidant formula: Asaya 15% Vitamin C + E + Ferulic**  
The combination of vitamin C, vitamin E and ferulic acid is appealing if pigmentation and overall photo-protection are your priorities; current listing is around ₹674. 

### How I'd use it

**Morning:** cleanser → 2–3 drops vitamin C → moisturiser → **SPF 50 sunscreen**.

Sunscreen is crucial: UV exposure can keep producing pigmentation while you're trying to fade existing spots. Visible improvement usually takes **several weeks rather than a few days**. If your skin is **sensitive, acne-prone, or easily gets irritated**, I'd choose the 10% option first. Irritation itself can worsen pigmentation.

If you tell me your **skin type (oily/dry/combination/sensitive), age, budget (e.g. ₹500/₹1,000), and whether the dark spots are acne marks or sun/upper-lip pigmentation**, I can narrow this to **one specific serum** for you.

sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
